The page is Nebraska form DC 1:15, whose caption block is a set of alternate captions the form's own script shows one at a time. Separately, ten underscore rules run past the right page edge (x1 = 613 on a 612pt page) on packet pages 4 and 5, where the source has one. The family holds a RASTER_PASS receipt; the raster gate proves the pages render, not that they can be read.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.detail: A real regression introduced by the fill step, which the visualDefects counter does not see (it reports 0). In all four cr-400-filled.pdf fixtures the Judicial Council's own footer sentence is damaged and runs off the left page edge. Measured with pdftotext -bbox on a 612x792 page: the official CR-400 source and the committed derived-sources/cr-400-pikepdf-unlocked.pdf both render that footer intact across two lines starting at x=36.00 — 'For'(36.0-48.9) 'your'(51.1-68.4) 'protection'(70.7-109.8) ... at y=757.8, then 'This Form button after you have printed the form.' at y=767.4 — and neither has any word outside the page box (minimum x0 = 36.00, 432 words each). The filled artifact has re-flowed that sentence onto a single line at y=766.0, DROPPED the words 'For' and 'your' entirely, TRUNCATED 'protection' to 'otection', and placed it at x0 = -3.485, i.e. 3.49pt off the left edge of the page (minimum x0 = -3.48, 436 words). A word-set diff confirms it: 'For' and 'protection' are present in the official and absent from the filled artifact; 'otection' is present in the filled artifact and absent from the official. reports/actual-writes.json records the mechanism in its own pdfLibWarnings — 'Removing XFA form data as pdf-lib does not support reading or writing XFA' — so the XFA-to-flattened-AcroForm conversion is re-laying out official furniture. reports/source-fidelity.json cannot catch this because it only compares official-to-derived (which is faithful), never derived-to-filled. Repair target: the CR-400 finalize/flatten path; the acceptance check needs to extend to the filled artifact. No same-baseline text-on-text overlap above 1pt was found in any of the twelve artifacts.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 amendment A1: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer. It does — packet-family-build-worklist.json records filingDestination as 'recorded': 'Superior Court of the county of conviction.', and CA.memo.json track ca-prop64 destination.name says the same. The packet states exactly that destination: 'Ask the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of the conviction.' Only the court's street ADDRESS is described as unheld, which is a different and true statement — no held record carries a per-county address. The destination itself is stated, not deferred.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001, asking first whether the repository establishes the answer. It does not: packet-family-build-worklist.json records filingFee status 'not_recorded'. The repository does hold 'FW-001 is the general California fee waiver form', but WAVE_2_LEGAL_INPUT_ASSIGNMENTS.json has already adjudicated exactly that point for this family — it names FW-001 'only as California's general fee-waiver form, which does not determine whether either §11361.8 filing has a fee or when a waiver is required. That exact legal input is absent.' So FW-001 is not an answer this packet is withholding. The packet states that the fee and waiver are not established and names a specific checkable authority — the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of the conviction — which is the determination's third 'met' branch. I record that I nearly failed this obligation on the FW-001 mention before reading the adjudication; demanding a figure the repository does not hold is the invention the determination forbids.

SERVICE.detail: The repository establishes who must be served and the packet tells the participant it does not. packet-family-build-worklist.json records serviceRecipients as status 'recorded' with the entry 'Serve the prosecuting agency and file CR-401 proof of service.', and certificateOfService as 'recorded': 'proof_of_service: CR-401'; CA.memo.json track ca-prop64 rules.service says the same and rules.notice adds 'The prosecuting agency responds at CR-402.' participant-instructions.md line 20 instead reads: 'The filing fee and whether it can be waived, who must be served and by what method, and the address of the court are not established in this repository.' The 'by what method' half of that sentence is true — serviceMethod and serviceTiming are both 'not_recorded' — but the 'who must be served' half is false against a held record, and the packet ships CR-401, the proof-of-service form, with a 25-row blank table while never saying whom it proves service on. This is amendment A1's defect one obligation over: substituting a question for an answer the repository already holds. Repair: state that the prosecuting agency is served and that CR-401 is the proof of service, and keep the honest refusal for method and timing, naming the clerk for those.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The packet states where it stops, in terms: 'This is where this packet's self-help ends: fee, waiver, service, and local filing practice come from the clerk of that court, not from this packet.' It also states which fields it will not complete ('The platform never marks a box on a sworn filing', 'Sign and date each form yourself', 'Leave CR-403 entirely blank'), and that the artifact carries no approval ('These files are deterministic review fixtures ... They are not approved filing packets').

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001. Asking first whether the repository establishes the answer: it does. The delivered form's printed instruction 1 states, in a parenthesis on its own face which I read from the fixture bytes: '(NOTE: There is no application fee.)' packet-family-build-worklist.json records filingFee as status 'recorded' for this family. The packet says so nowhere; its only cost sentence is the catch-all 'Confirm ... fees ... before filing', which is the determination's second notMet branch — a gesture at a fee without naming who answers it. This also bears on the family's queue status: MASTER_QUEUE carries legalInputStatus OPEN_LEGAL_INPUT on the basis of 'fee and waiver treatment', but the fee for this route is answered by the held source on its own face, so this is a packet-content defect to repair rather than an open legal input to wait on. I record the disagreement and did not edit MASTER_QUEUE.

SERVICE.detail: Silence, and not the honest kind. packet-family-build-worklist.json records serviceRecipients, serviceMethod, certificateOfService and notice all as 'not_recorded', so no held source establishes a service rule — which under the determination means the packet may stand on a NAMED checkable authority instead. It names none. All it offers is 'Complete service certificates only after service actually occurs' and the same catch-all 'Confirm ... service ... before filing': no office, no desk, no clerk the participant could actually reach. That is the determination's notMet branch, and true silence fails. There is more to say than that, too: item 6 of the form's own court-use-only checklist, read from the bytes here, is 'Copies of application sent to prosecutor, law enforcement agencies and DCJS as applicable for further processing' — the COURT distributes, so the participant plausibly serves nobody, and the packet could state that affirmatively with the mechanism that replaces service. Repair: either state that the participant serves nobody and the court distributes, or name the court of conviction as the authority to ask.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The packet states which fields it will not complete ('Court, judge, prosecutor, clerk, law-enforcement, agency, notary, hearing, and post-order fields remain for their proper owners'), that it carries no approval ('These files are deterministic review fixtures ... They are not approved filing packets'), and that it grants no branch selection ('This artifact covers only an explicitly requested irreversible-destruction branch and grants no runtime permission to select it'). Scored PASS on its own terms; note that the same file's court-only-fields defect scored under REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING cuts against the boundary this section draws.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.detail: The packet's own 'facts you must supply before filing' list omits obligations the repository marks required before filing, including one the record says defeats the petition. Scored under A2's test — ask first whether the repository establishes the answer — applied to the obligation the packet's own section is named after. The committed packet-set manifest for ut_pet_conviction-set carries a requiredBeforeFiling array, and A2's answersVT8C4 settles that a committed manifest's participantActionRequired entries are a held source. Missing from the delivered instructions: (1) 'Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a current balance … and check with the Office of State Debt Collection … An unpaid balance defeats the petition and will also defeat the BCI certificate' — no trace of it anywhere in the 6,356-byte file; (2) 'List every criminal case you have ever had, in any state, including cases that were already expunged. BCI reviews all of them when it decides your certificate' — the manifest's own note is that 'an incomplete list produces a denial rather than a certificate'. Everything the field map itself declares IS disclosed: I applied the disclosure gate by hand to all twelve rows carrying approvedBlankDisposition REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, because the committed reader never runs it here, and all twelve are named in the instructions — judicial district and court address, BCI certificate number, the public-interest explanation, previously used names, gender, SSN and driver licence, and the signing block. So the failure is not about form blanks; it is that the packet's pre-filing section is scoped to blanks on paper while the repository's is scoped to what the participant must have in hand, and the difference includes a money bar that kills the petition. FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Scored under A1: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer, and it does — the committed track registry gives 'Stage two: expungement petition in the court that entered the conviction … in the court that decided the case', and the packet now states it. The instructions name both destinations in order: 'The Utah Bureau of Criminal Identification (BCI)' for stage one and 'The Utah district court for the county where the case was heard' for stage two, with the 180-day window between them and the observation that the judicial district number and the court's street address remain the participant's to write. Every quotation is sourced and I verified each against the held bytes with pdftotext: UT-BCI-EXP-INSTRUCTIONS prints 'File a Cover Sheet, Petition to Expunge and Order on Petition to Expunge with the appropriate court', 'You will take this list to the court that is listed for that case', and 'You have 180 Days (including weekends and holidays) from the date listed on the letter of Expungement Eligibility to petition the court(s)'. This is the obligation MASTER_QUEUE still records as FAILED on a 1,167-byte file with no filing section at all; that record is stale. QUALIFICATION FOR THE CAPTAIN, recorded rather than scored: the repository says 'the court that decided the case', and both the track registry and the packet-set manifest add 'district or justice court'. The packet names only the district court and pre-marks the District box on the delivered petition and order, and the packet is built on 1044XX, which is the DISTRICT court cover sheet. That is internally coherent, but the route admits class B misdemeanours and infractions, which Utah justice courts decide, and the packet tells such a participant nothing. It is a route-scope question rather than a silence, so I record it here instead of failing the obligation.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A2, and the packet fails on the limb A2 was written for: its claim about its own bound FORMS is right and its claim about the REPOSITORY is false. What the repair got right, and I verified: the court filing fee is stated and sourced — 'The court filing fee is $150', drawn from 1044XX page 2, and pdftotext -bbox on the official 1044XX confirms the row '$150 [ ] Expungement Petition - Criminal (E)' is on page 2 and that the packet marks that exact box; and the waiver route is named with a real instrument, form 1305GE 'Motion to Waive Fees for Expungement – Criminal', which I extracted from the held PDF and which carries exactly the title, the Utah Code 78A-2-302 citation and the Rule 4-508 citation the packet gives. WHAT FAILS. The packet then says: 'The BCI certificate carries a separate fee, and this packet does not state an amount because BCI sets it per applicant.' The repository does state one, and so does the packet's own paper. Page 17 of the delivered canonical.pdf — which is UT-BCI-EXP-APPLICATION source page 1, and which I read out of the fixture bytes, not the corpus copy — prints 'The application fee is $65.00 and non-refundable.' Page 18 prints it twice more: 'accompanied by a non-refundable $65.00 application fee' and 'Application fee is $65.00'. Stage one of the two-stage route this packet describes therefore has a flat, printed, held fee of $65.00 and the packet tells the participant no amount exists. There are two BCI money items and the packet conflates them: the $65.00 application fee, which is fixed and held, and the per-incident certificate purchase price, which genuinely is set per applicant in the BCI letter and which the packet is right to refuse. Refusing the second does not license denying the first. The repair is a sentence: state $65.00 for the application, keep the honest refusal for the certificates, and keep the named authority. Also recorded: the delivered BCI page carries a sequencing rule the packet omits — 'If you believe you are indigent and you check the box … you MUST complete the fee waiver form before submitting your application' — where the packet only says to ask BCI whether you qualify. APPLIED A3 (read from the captain head; it postdates this row's base). A3 asks whether the record establishes the fact FOR THIS ROUTE. Both figures here pass that test at the shortest possible range, because neither comes from a shared jurisdiction table: the $65.00 is printed on the face of UT-BCI-EXP-APPLICATION, which is a bound component of THIS packet and the stage-one instrument of THIS route, and I read it out of this family's own delivered fixture bytes at packet pages 17 and 18 rather than from any profile; the $150 is the row of 1044XX that the packet itself marks, captioned 'Expungement Petition - Criminal (E)', on a cover sheet that is likewise a bound component of this packet. There is no sibling-route line in play on either. A3 therefore leaves this failure exactly where it was.

SERVICE.detail: The packet states the recipient, the method and a named checkable authority, all sourced, so it is met on the determination's first limb — and there is a repository conflict underneath it that the Captain should see. WHAT THE PACKET SAYS: 'The prosecutor must receive a copy of what you file, by mail or by email', citing BCI's Expungement Applicant Instructions, plus form 1146XX for the prosecutor to acknowledge receipt, the objection-and-hearing possibility, the Utah State Courts Self-Help Center on 888-583-0009, and the rule that the service method, address and date are completed only after service actually happens. VERIFIED AT SOURCE: I extracted UT-BCI-EXP-INSTRUCTIONS (rehashed to 9e03980f…) and its Step 2 is headed 'File the petition with the court and serve the Prosecutor' and its third bullet reads, verbatim, 'Mail or email the prosecutor copies of what you file'; the Self-Help Center number 888-583-0009 is printed in the same step. MASTER_QUEUE still records this obligation as FAILED for the 1,167-byte file; that record is stale. THE CONFLICT, recorded not resolved: two other held records say the opposite. The committed track registry's stage-two unit says 'The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve', the committed route census repeats it as this route's serviceRecipients and serviceMethod, and the committed packet-set manifest's serve_party says 'The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case … The Proof of Service form appears in the published packet only as an optional form, used where the prosecutor's office will not accept service.' So the repository holds one answer twice and the official publication holds the other. Under AGENTS.md's source hierarchy the official Utah source governs and the packet followed it, which is also the safer instruction to give a participant; the registry and census entries are the fidelity defect. I did not edit them.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The packet states what it will not do and carries no approval. It opens 'This is a review fixture built from exact held official Utah forms', closes with 'This is a prepared set of official Utah forms built for review. It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether the court will grant expungement', and draws the ownership line explicitly: 'Signatures, signature dates, service certifications, court-only fields, agency-only fields, prosecutor-only fields, victim fields, and optional third-party authorizations remain protected.' It refuses to assert eligibility for the BCI waiver ('do not assume the court's $150 waiver covers BCI's fee, because they are two different offices'). approval-request.json is REQUESTED with grantedBy null, independentVisualReviewRequired and outputLegalApprovalRequired both true, and product-wiring.json carries generationAllowed false, runtimeSelectable false, commercialRoutesOpened 0, createsFulfillmentRecord false. Cross-reference: the FEE_AND_WAIVER failure above is a place where the packet asserts an absence it should not have asserted, which cuts against the honesty this section claims, but the boundary this obligation measures is drawn correctly.

caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.theAuditsClaimIsWrongOnScope: An audit reported 40 fields across 4 families and nothing else anywhere in the corpus. Measured here the true figure is 48 fields across 5 families: ca-1203-41-set 10, ca-1203-42-set 10, ca-1203-43-set 10, ca-1203-4a-set 10 and ca-17b-reduction-set 8. The declarations appear identically in both field-census.census-v1.json and production-field-map.json in each of the five. The audit's 40/4 is the four families it did not hold; the fifth, ca-17b-reduction-set, is the held family, and it declares 8 more. Outside those five nothing declares it: the only other mention in the repository is scripts/build-census-v1-az_marijuana_expungement_arrest_no_charges-set.mjs, which is the shared West-family builder that emits and validates the flag, and no Arizona overlay declares it.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.theCaptionClaimIsCorrect: The audit's claim that every declaring field carries the printed caption 'eligible for reduction' is TRUE, and it survives the trap that the field NAMES do not say so. Half the declaring fields are named Offense1..Offense5, which reads like an offence-description column. Measured from CR-180's own printed words with pdftotext -bbox against each widget rect: the header at x333-446 reads 'Eligible for reduction to misdemeanor under Penal Code, § 17(b) (yes or no)' and the widgets under it are Reduce1..Reduce5 at x331.63-447.3; the header at x454-570 reads 'Eligible for reduction to infraction under Penal Code, § 17(d)(2) (yes or no)' and the widgets under it are Offense1..Offense5 at x453.6-569.27. The OffenseN name is a Judicial Council misnomer and the printed caption governs. No field declaring the exception is route-determined; both columns ask a characterisation of the listed offence under Penal Code § 17, and the petition reads identically whichever way each resolves.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.eachDeclaredCellIsNamed: For each of ca-1203-42-set, ca-1203-43-set and ca-1203-4a-set, all 10 declared cells appear in participant-instructions.md with their page and the printed caption, and a dedicated section headed '10 of those blanks are yours even though they read like an election' quotes the recorded reason and adds the instruction that matters: answer only for offences actually listed, from the participant's own record of conviction, and 'if you do not know whether an offence is reducible, that is a question for a lawyer or a legal-aid office and not one to guess at, because you sign this petition under penalty of perjury.' The blanks did not merely move; they were named.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.thePacketDoesNotAnswerTheQuestion: Verified in the bytes, not the declaration. A 150dpi ink diff of every CR-180 page in ca-1203-42-set against derived-sources/cr-180-pikepdf-unlocked.pdf finds no added ink anywhere in the ConvTable region, on any of the five rows, in either column. Every checkbox-sized added cluster on pages 1-3 was rendered individually at 300dpi and is an empty flattened border. The packet text contains no yes/no answer to the § 17(b) or § 17(d)(2) question.
caseDeterminedExceptionAudit.theHeldFamilyIsHeldForTheRightReason: ca-17b-reduction-set is not mine and I did not verify it, but it is the control that makes the exception legible and it was measured in the same pass. Its ConvTable Row1 carries Reduce1=WRITE and Offense1=WRITE while Rows 2-5 carry {Code, Section, TypeOff, Reduce, Offense} all blank. That is the packet answering the § 17 question for row 1 on a petition sworn under penalty of perjury, and matching one row's writes to four rows' blanks. It is also why it declares 8 rather than 10. FEE_AND_WAIVER.evidence: The packet states: 'Ask the clerk what fee applies. The fee for a petition to annul is not established in any source this packet holds, so it is not stated here.' The waiver half is answered - NHJB-2311 with NHJB-2328 are named and prepared. The fee half is not, and the platform holds the figure: NH.memo.json rules.fees for this track states '$125.00 per court location', and destination.detail repeats 'petitions filed at the same time in one court location share a single $125.00 filing fee.' The packet's sentence is literally true of its OWN bindings - the NH source receipt binds only the four form binaries and carries no groundingRecords, and scripts/build-census-v1-nh_petition_vacated-set.mjs reads no legal-design record - but the obligation is that the fee is stated, and a filing packet sends the participant to the clerk for a number the platform already holds. Contrast CO in this same cohort, where the identical sentence is accurate because CO.memo records that the source review states no filing fee; the difference is why this is booked as a defect here and not there. On THIS track the omission is heavier, because the fee position is the entire reason the track exists as a separate node. NH.memo's legalDesignDecision says so: it is 'kept as a separate node rather than merged into that track because the fee position differs: the RSA 651:5, IX and X(d) exemptions are written around not-guilty, dismissed and not-prosecuted cases and on the face of the statute do not reach a vacated conviction, which is a real cost difference the participant must be told about before filing.' rules.fees adds that whether the $100 Department of Corrections investigation fee and the Department of Safety and state police fees apply is unresolved and 'on the face of the statute the exemptions do not reach a vacated conviction, so the packet should assume they are payable.' The packet tells the participant none of this: its fee paragraph is byte-identical to the non-conviction family's, which is the one family for which the exemptions DO apply. The single fact the controlling record says must be disclosed before filing on this route is the one fact the packet does not carry.

ARTIFACTS.finding: THE REPRODUCIBILITY DRIFT, MEASURED HERE RATHER THAN CARRIED FROM FIX51, AND RULED A NOTE RATHER THAN AN ARTIFACTS FAILURE. The committed fixtures carry a wall clock in their document metadata - canonical /ModDate and /CreationDate (D:20260901085519Z), boundary (D:20260901085542Z), two different timestamps 23 seconds apart - while the builder stamps stampDeterministic() = RCAP_PACKET_PDF_DATE (D:20260829000000Z) into both entries, which is what the sibling trafficking fixtures carry. Measured WITHOUT rebuilding, so that no overlay byte was touched: substituting only those date strings in the committed bytes yields canonical 3db619bfe92cf022bef8eceed5391cb3d26a042d42ea5545d561e098e0bcac58 and boundary 0cd742adf07eda692e74e56854a32824f03ea9102a92c79d3076a0761d020f97, at unchanged byte lengths - exactly the digests FIX51's clean-tree control build produced. So the entire difference between the committed fixtures and what this builder now emits is the two date strings, and not one glyph, widget, appearance or page differs. The magnitude is 16 bytes per fixture, 8 in /ModDate and 8 in /CreationDate, 32 across the family - FIX51 reported '16 bytes across the two files, 8 in each, and they are the /ModDate', which is half the count and misses /CreationDate; its conclusion is confirmed, its measurement is understated. RULING on the contract: ARTIFACTS asks whether the canonical and boundary bytes hash to what the record names, and they do, to every record that names them; date metadata is not ink and no page differs, so this is not an ARTIFACTS failure at this base. It is a determinism hazard the Captain owns: any rebuild of this family moves both digests on the date alone and would discard a RASTER_PASS bound to bytes nobody changed, which is the exact harm rcap-deterministic-pdf-date.mjs exists to prevent. Normalising it is a re-raster, not an instructions repair, and FIX51 was right to restore rather than leave it moved.

The delivered appearance regenerated over the write draws a rectangle instead: /FlatWidget-578830786 opens '0 0 0 RG / 1 w / [] 0 d / 1 0 0 1 0.5 0.5 cm' and strokes '0 0 m / 0 14.043 l / 163.45 14.043 l / 163.45 0 l / h / S'. IN INK, AND ATTRIBUTED: on rule-790-order-canonical page 1 the Defendant /Rect carries 2764 packet-only dark pixels along its top edge, 240 along its left and 244 along its right -- three sides the form does not draw -- 3172 in the 2pt perimeter ring in total; DocketNumber carries 2707, 298 and 244, 3166 in the ring. On rule-790-order-boundary the same DocketNumber box is present, 3166; its Defendant box is absent only because that value was refused as unfittable and no appearance was regenerated. 9504 packet-only dark pixels across the two order fixtures, none of which appears in the pinned form as published or in its page content with annotations removed. The two boxed fields are the petitioner's NAME and the DOCKET NUMBER in the caption of the proposed order the packet tells the participant to hand up to a judge, and on the boundary fixture the docket text sits 0.5pt from the drawn left rule. THIS IS THE SHARED-HOST DEFECT THE ASSIGNMENT NAMED, AND I CHECKED THE SIBLING RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT: rule-490-order-canonical.pdf in data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1/pa/pa-490-nonconviction-set--official-pdf-fill/fixtures carries the identical '0 0 0 RG ... 1 0 0 1 0.5 0.5 cm ... 0 0 m' signature on its own written fields. PA 790's order shows it. The petition does not and cannot: its own /MK dictionaries are empty, with no /BC, so no border is regenerated there, and the pixel measurement agrees. WHAT IS SOUND, MEASURED AND NOT SCORED AGAINST THE PACKET. (1) Zero source pixels are missing on any of the six official pages, so nothing is overpainted. (2) The five synthesized squares the prior read scored are gone: petition Checkbox2 in both states and order Checkbox1, Checkbox2 and Checkbox3 each add 0 dark pixels in every fixture. (3) Packet-owned added ink lying OUTSIDE every declared write rectangle is 0 on all six official pages -- measured as delivered AND NOT published AND NOT the stripped page content, with each declared write rectangle padded 1pt. (4) The two petition 'Check Box1' widgets add 298 and 384 pixels against the pinned form as published, and 100 per cent of that is the SOURCE'S OWN: in those two windows the delivered ink is EXACTLY the union of the published form's ink and the form's own page content, zero pixels either way, in both fixtures -- the widget's /Off appearance opens with an opaque white fill that hides part of the form's printed box, the shared background neutralization strips it, and the form's own box shows through. Nothing there is the packet's. (5) Every one of the 32 declared writes was isolated (its own added ink, with every other declared rectangle masked out) and measured against its own /Rect: no glyph overflows, the tightest margin that is not the border stroke is -0.136pt on the petition boundary's Addr2, which is the antialiased descender edge at just over half a pixel. (6) The composed certificates carry ink only between 72.24pt and 527.52pt horizontally and 64.80pt and 396.24pt from the top of a 612 x 792pt page, so nothing is clipped and nothing reaches a margin, in either fixture.

SERVICE.evidence: Who must be served and when is stated, verbatim from the record, and what is genuinely unestablished is confined to what is genuinely unestablished. whyTheseAreNotRows.currentAppendNote: The prose below was written for the original eight refusals and is preserved as historical explanation. ca-851-91-set is the ninth current claim-gate refusal and is kept outside rows for the same non-supersession reason.
whyTheseAreNotRows.what: These eight refusals are recorded here and NOT appended to the rows array, deliberately.
whyTheseAreNotRows.why: extract-verifier-returns.mjs reads every entry in rows as a verdict ABOUT THE FAMILY and keeps one current verdict per family. Its supersedes() prefers a row whose declared verifiedAtBase is a descendant of the incumbent's. All eight of these families currently carry FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED at bases 7fcfb7d40aafe7bd7350fc735ea09d16524cb757, ebc44031ec7eab29058bfc79a7bc5e1cff089414 and 36d7718a7e48d7f87f18eeaf3b18ed9b3ce545c8; git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms each is an ancestor of this base. A row of mine declaring this base would therefore have superseded all eight.
whyTheseAreNotRows.measuredConsequence: The baseline sweep at this base reports 32 FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED families and names all eight of these among them. Appending these refusals as rows would have taken that list to 24 — eight known-failing families dropped off the repair queue on the strength of a read that never happened, replaced by a verdict that is a statement about this lane rather than about the packet.
whyTheseAreNotRows.therefore: A claim-gate refusal is not a verdict about a family and is not recorded as one. rows is left exactly as the previous lanes wrote it; nothing was superseded, upgraded, downgraded or removed.
whyTheseAreNotRows.aStructuralFindingForCaptain: The extractor has no way to say 'this lane could not look'. Its vocabulary contains BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM and STOPPED, but any row carrying them still competes for the family's single current-verdict slot and still displaces an actionable FAIL. If refused lanes are expected to return rows, the extractor should exclude non-reading verdicts from supersession. Raised, not decided, and not repaired here: this lane may not edit factory scripts.
whyTheseAreNotRows.alsoChecked: All fifteen obligation names already appear in each of these four documents, so adding them here leaves unscoredObligations empty as it already was, and no other lane's PASS_COMPLETE_INDEPENDENT row changes its downgrade state.

sharedToolingFinding.title: Whole-file SHA-256 pins on shared national records go stale whenever any other jurisdiction is amended
sharedToolingFinding.scope: cross-family, not specific to any family this cohort read
sharedToolingFinding.measured: Every source-receipt.json under data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1 was scanned at base 5de917b3574b6e27df362e13b86b4bfaac4915f8 and every pinned repository record recomputed with sha256. 233 receipts; 45 pins; 35 recompute equal; 10 are stale, spread over 10 families.

twoRecordsAccountForAllTen.data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet: 7 stale pins, 0 current. Amended 8 times in the history reachable here; receipts across the census pin 4 different historical digests of it (80d88d69..., 563147bf..., 713ed7ab..., 6076f734...), and only 6076f734... is the file today.
twoRecordsAccountForAllTen.data/rcap-ledger/completed-output-counse: 3 stale pins, 0 current. Pinned at 99e80291... (commit eab70f926); current is fbf9bfef... (commit cb6cbf45e), whose only delta to the file is one added Kansas route entry.

sharedToolingFinding.whyItHappens: Both records are national and are amended in place as each new jurisdiction is productized. A per-family receipt that pins the whole file therefore fails the moment an unrelated state is added, even though the family's own entry is untouched. I confirmed for both families in this cohort that the family's own entry is byte-identical between the pinned commit and this base, so no legal statement moved.
sharedToolingFinding.whyItMatters: SOURCE IDENTITY is stated as an exact recomputation, so a verifier that measures it honestly must fail these families, and a repair lane must re-pin. The re-pin then goes stale again on the next unrelated amendment. Two of this cohort's six FAIL-bearing obligations are this defect and nothing else.
sharedToolingFinding.suggestedDurableFix: Pin the family's own subtree of a shared national record - the packetSetId entry, the route entry - rather than the whole file, or record the pin as {commit, path, selector, subtreeDigest}. Either makes the binding survive amendments to other jurisdictions while still failing if the family's own legal content changes. This is a decision for a tooling or Captain lane; this cohort verifies and does not repair.
sharedToolingFinding.whatThisIsNot: Not a defect in the two records themselves, not a legal-content change, and not grounds to re-render any fixture. Every affected family here is bound by a hash-bound RASTER_PASS receipt to the bytes on disk, and re-rendering would cost it that gate for a receipt-field correction.
